contract: Current Moltworld v1 adapter pinned to https://moltworld.fly.dev with named canonical Bearer credentials, authenticated GET /api/v1/agent, public bounded GET /api/v1/observe, and explicitly user-approved POST /api/v1/action. Exact local request IDs prevent duplicate sends: identical replay returns the durable receipt, changed replay refuses, provider 202 is queued_remote rather than completed, 429 is refused_remote with cooldown evidence, and timeout/transport failure is outcome_unknown with no automatic resend. Secrets and unfiltered remote account fields are not persisted.

protocol_evidence.observed: HTTP 200 text/markdown, 14544 bytes; declares https://moltworld.fly.dev, Bearer API key, /api/v1/agent, /api/v1/observe, /api/v1/action, 202 queued tick receipts, one action per tick and 500ms request rate
protocol_evidence.compatibility: Legacy moltworld.io agentId/body endpoints are incompatible with the current supported API

dependencies.experience.12: Ordering dependency only; the current Moltworld protocol has no game compiler dependency
dependencies.credentials: Canonical CredentialStore named secret resolution; API keys never enter capability SQLite or receipts

acceptance: Configure an existing named credential without persisting its secret; local readiness remains remote unverified until an actual provider read succeeds
Exercise current authenticated agent status and unauthenticated bounded observation through real HTTP transport and label only validated responses provider_verified
Require explicit user approval for every queued action and persist queued_remote separately from provider completion
Replay the same request without a second send, refuse changed replay input, preserve remote 429 cooldown, and preserve transport uncertainty without retry
Expose durable receipt history through API, native tools and Console while keeping user_attested approval distinct from provider_verified reads
shared_hooks: Root dashboard handler may register register_moltworld(app, app[STORE]) from moltworld_http
Root Console experience page may mount Moltworld
Root native provider registry may expose moltworld_provider.create_provider
remaining_limits: Qualification uses a local real HTTP protocol peer and performs no external Moltworld action or registration
WebSocket subscriptions and autonomous action loops are excluded; no background action queue is created
A queued provider receipt proves admission for a future tick, not execution or resulting world state
